Reliability profile at a fixed between-site SD

Source: R/class-reliability-profile.R, R/accessors.R, R/draws.R, and 1 more
reliability_profile.Rd

Computes the site reliabilities and the diagnostics of their profile at a given between-site standard deviation: a planning value, the true value of a simulation, or an estimate from another fit.

Usage

reliability_profile(x = NULL, ...)

# Default S3 method
reliability_profile(
  x = NULL,
  ...,
  se = NULL,
  se2 = NULL,
  sigma_tau,
  site = NULL,
  estimate = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  scale_label = NULL,
  target_label = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
reliability_profile(
  x,
  ...,
  se = NULL,
  se2 = NULL,
  sigma_tau,
  site = NULL,
  estimate = NULL,
  scale_label = NULL,
  target_label = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_profile'
update(object, ..., sigma_tau = NULL, scale_label = NULL, target_label = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_posterior'
reliability_profile(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_draws'
reliability_profile(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_profile'
format(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_profile'
print(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_profile'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.reliability_profile'
format(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'summary.reliability_profile'
print(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_profile'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

Usually left out, with the standard errors given as se or se2. It can also be a data frame, in which se, se2, site and estimate name columns; a posterior fit or posterior draws, for the profile at the posterior mean of \(\sigma_\tau^2\); or a fit of metafor, ebnm or multisiteDGP (see metafor-methods, ebnm-methods and multisitedgp-methods).

...

Must be empty.

se

Standard errors of the site estimates, a numeric vector of positive numbers. With a data frame x, an unquoted column name. Give se or se2, not both.

se2

Sampling variances of the site estimates, as se.

sigma_tau

Standard deviation of the true effects across sites, a number of at least 0.

site

Optional labels of the sites, one for each site and all distinct. With a data frame x, an unquoted column name.

estimate

Optional estimates of the sites, a numeric vector. When they are given, the site table also has the posterior mean and standard deviation of each site's effect at sigma_tau.

data

Optional data frame in which se, se2, site and estimate are found, as in reliability_posterior(); the same as giving the data frame as x.

scale_label, target_label

Optional strings that name the scale of the effects, such as "risk difference" (read as "on the risk difference scale"), and the estimand at each site, such as "the block-adjusted intention-to-treat contrast for course passing". They appear in the printed output and in report_text().

object

A profile made by reliability_profile().

use_cli

Whether to print the headings in bold with the cli package, when it is installed. NULL, the default, takes getOption("poolinfo.use_cli", TRUE).

row.names, optional

Ignored.

Value

An object of class reliability_profile, a list with components

  • se2, site and estimate (or NULL): the data.

  • X: the mean-model matrix inherited from a fitted model, or NULL for a common mean.

  • sigma_tau and source: the between-site SD and where it came from.

  • S: the reliabilities.

  • stats: a named vector of the diagnostics: I, mean, harmonic, H, V, rho3 (the third absolute moment of the centered logits), J_eff, gap (the mean reliability minus \(I\)), benchmark_risk (see benchmark_risk()), trace (the sum of the reliabilities), v_typ (the typical variance of typical_variance()) and R_typ (the reliability at that variance).

  • local: the table of local_terms().

  • labels: the scale and estimand labels.

  • call and version: the call and the version of the package that made the profile.

It has methods for print(), summary(), as.data.frame() (the site table), plot() and update().

Details

With sampling variances \(v_j\) and the between-site standard deviation \(\sigma_\tau\), the reliability of site \(j\) is \(S_j = \sigma_\tau^2/(\sigma_\tau^2 + v_j)\). The profile's diagnostics are the informativeness \(I\) (kl_centroid()), the mean reliability, the harmonic centroid, the dispersion \(H\) (kl_dispersion()), the logit variance \(V\) (logit_moments()), the concentration count \(J_{\mathrm{eff}}\) (concentration_count()) and the terms of local_terms(). summary() adds the benchmark risk, the sum of the reliabilities and the typical variance of typical_variance().

This is the profile at one value of sigma_tau. When sigma_tau is estimated from the same data, reliability_posterior() averages the diagnostics over its posterior distribution instead, which is what we recommend for reporting. Profiles obtained from a posterior or a metafor fit with moderators retain its mean-model matrix. Their site effects pool toward the site's fitted mean, with uncertainty in the mean-model coefficients integrated out under a flat prior.

At sigma_tau = 0 every reliability is 0 and the profile is a limit: \(I\), the mean reliability and \(H\) are 0, and the concentration count is its limit \((\sum_j v_j^{-1})^2 / \sum_j v_j^{-2}\), and a message is shown.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

See also

profile_summary() and site_table() for the numbers as data frames, reliability_posterior() for the posterior over sigma_tau, and vignette("reliability-profiles") for what the diagnostics describe.

Examples

se <- c(0.10, 0.12, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30)
prof <- reliability_profile(se = se, sigma_tau = 0.2)
prof
#> Reliability profile of 6 sites at sigma_tau = 0.2 (supplied)
#> 
#>   informativeness I            0.571
#>   mean reliability             0.562
#>   dispersion H                 0.0720
#>   logit variance V             0.609
#>   concentration count J_eff    5.5 of 6
#> 
#> Site reliabilities range from 0.31 to 0.80.
summary(prof)
#> Reliability profile of 6 sites at sigma_tau = 0.2 (supplied)
#> 
#> Centroids
#>   harmonic centroid            0.501    (harmonic mean)
#>   informativeness I            0.571    (logit mean)
#>   mean reliability             0.562    (arithmetic mean)
#> 
#> Dispersion and concentration
#>   dispersion H                 0.0720
#>   logit variance V             0.609
#>   concentration count J_eff    5.5 of 6
#> 
#> Second-order terms (Lee, 2026)
#>                                                           leading term
#>                           exact      leading    bound     decides the sign
#>   H                       0.0720     0.0746     0.00933   -
#>   mean reliability - I   -0.00922   -0.0107     0.0121    no
#> 
#> Related summaries
#>   benchmark risk sigma_tau^2 (1 - mean S_j)    0.0175
#>   sum of reliabilities                         3.4
#>   typical variance (Higgins-Thompson)          0.0251   R_typ 0.614

# The same from a data frame, with the columns named
dat <- data.frame(school = letters[1:6], y = c(0.3, 0.1, 0.25, -0.05, 0.4, 0),
                  s = se)
reliability_profile(dat, se = s, estimate = y, site = school, sigma_tau = 0.2)
#> Reliability profile of 6 sites at sigma_tau = 0.2 (supplied)
#> 
#>   informativeness I            0.571
#>   mean reliability             0.562
#>   dispersion H                 0.0720
#>   logit variance V             0.609
#>   concentration count J_eff    5.5 of 6
#> 
#> Site reliabilities range from 0.31 to 0.80.

# The profile at another sigma_tau
update(prof, sigma_tau = 0.1)
#> Reliability profile of 6 sites at sigma_tau = 0.1 (supplied)
#> 
#>   informativeness I            0.250
#>   mean reliability             0.276
#>   dispersion H                 0.0565
#>   logit variance V             0.609
#>   concentration count J_eff    4.7 of 6
#> 
#> Site reliabilities range from 0.10 to 0.50.
